title: Required content should follow the profile's reference shape: conceptId#anchor requires that section, a bare conceptId the whole document (DEC-194 (5))
description:
DEC-194 (5) follow-up (opum-ai/opum-doc#1030), sequenced AFTER LCLI-722's cap PR (opum-ai/lore-cli#592). Deliberately NOT changed in that PR, on the leader's ruling.

WHAT IS WRONG TODAY. In the evidence tier, required content is matched by `conceptId` ALONE — the `ordered.filter((candidate) => candidate.conceptId === constitutionId)` set in `src/core/agent-context.ts`. EVERY candidate of that concept is therefore required, so a profile that RANKS the bundle's Constitution requires the WHOLE document, every section of it. That is not intended as a default: under DEC-194 (1)'s "pin sections, not documents", required content should mean what the profile PINS — a bare `conceptId` pins the whole document, and `conceptId#anchor` pins that section alone.

WHY IT MATTERS. Both reservations that landed with LCLI-722 — against the `task_evidence` cap and against the pack's `max_tokens` — size required content from that set. A profile that ranks the Constitution but wants one section of it therefore reserves, and can fail for, the whole document. The reservations are correct; the SET they reserve for is too wide. A whole Constitution is also what makes `CONTEXT_REQUIRED_CONTENT_OVER_BUDGET` reachable at a small `max_tokens`, when a single anchored section would have fitted.

WHAT TO DO. Make required content follow the profile's own reference shape. A `pinned`/`sources` entry that is a bare concept id keeps exactly the whole-document semantics it has today; an entry carrying `#anchor` requires THAT SECTION only. The required set then holds the anchored candidates, and `requiredTokens` sizes what the profile actually asked for rather than the whole document.

PROVE BOTH WAYS. A profile ranking `constitution#<section>` reserves and keeps only that section, while a profile ranking the bare `constitution` still reserves the whole document (the present behaviour, pinned so the change does not silently widen or narrow it). And a profile whose ANCHORED required section fits compiles, where the whole document would not. MUTATION CONTROL: widen the required set back to the bare `conceptId` and confirm the anchored-fits case goes red.

SEQUENCING AND THE STANDING CHECK. After LCLI-722's cap PR lands. If any of the four real profiles throws because a whole Constitution is required, THAT is this task's fix and not a raised budget — reported at filing as NOT currently the case: all four real profiles compile (documentation, implementation, review, verification), measured after the DEC-194 (5) reservations landed, so this task is a correctness-of-semantics change rather than a gate that is red today.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A ranked constitution#governance reserves and keeps ONLY that section.
At one task_evidence cap the anchored reference compiles while the bare constitution is refused by name with CONTEXT_REQUIRED_CONTENT_OVER_BUDGET, with the positive control in the same invocation.
A ranked bare constitution still reserves the WHOLE document when the cap can hold it, pinned so the behaviour cannot silently narrow.
The anchored reservation is the section size while the same document is an order of magnitude larger, so the cap is genuinely binding.
Mutation control: with the candidate producer anchor ignored, exactly the anchored arms redden and the bare arm stays green.
The measurement falsifying the filed premise is recorded on this task with the shapes and numbers.
A source comment at the required filter records that its input is already anchor-shaped, so the premise is not re-derived.
bun run lore check exits 0 on the branch head.
The full test suite, typecheck and lint are green on the pushed head.

plan: 1. Measure the filed premise against the real compile path before changing anything.
2. Build the proof the ruling asks for: rank an anchored Constitution section and a bare Constitution over a lopsided document, pinned both ways.
3. Run the mutation control from the DEFECT shape (the candidate producer ignoring its anchor) and confirm the predicted subset reddens.
4. Record the measurement at the required filter so the false premise is not re-derived.
5. Gates and delivery: bun run lore check, bun test, typecheck, lint; open the PR; complete the task on the branch.
implementationNotes: MEASUREMENT FALSIFYING THE FILED PREMISE, taken before any code was written. The defect this task describes - a profile that RANKS the bundle Constitution requires the WHOLE document, so an anchored reference still reserves every section - does NOT reproduce. requiredTokens, read from the CONTEXT_REQUIRED_CONTENT_OVER_BUDGET error or from a successful compile at a 1-token cap, over a Constitution whose whole document is ~3206 tokens, whose "## Governance" section is ~60 and whose "## Principles" is ~3111: sources [constitution] = 3206; sources [constitution#governance] = 60; sources [constitution#principles] = 3111; sources [specs/ui] = 0; pinned [constitution#governance] + sources [specs/ui] = 0; pinned [constitution] + sources [specs/ui] = 0; pinned [] with the auto-pin + sources [specs/ui] = 0. Eleven reference shapes measured in total. And the anchored-fits pair the ruling itself names, at the SAME 700-token task_evidence cap: sources [constitution] FAILS with requiredTokens 3202, while sources [constitution#governance] COMPILES holding one 56-token section. WHY: the filter is keyed on candidate.conceptId === constitutionId, but its INPUT is already anchor-shaped, because buildSourceCandidates builds each source candidates through regionForReference(concept.body, reference.anchor) (agent-context.ts:1706). The filer read the filter and not the candidate PRODUCER. CONSEQUENCE: WHAT TO DO is already the behaviour, so a faithful implementation is a NO-OP and the mutation control cannot be run as written - todays code IS the widened form that control names. THE ONE REAL GAP, which needed a ruling and did not get one here: the descriptions other sentence ("required content should mean what the profile PINS") is inconsistent with its own prove-both-ways clause, and the only behavioural delta that reading produces is the PINNED tier, which contributes 0 to required even when it pins the whole document. Routed to the orchestrator as a design question; NO production change was made in this branch. DELIVERED HERE: the proof the ruling asks for, both ways, plus a source comment recording where the semantics actually live.

RULING RECEIVED, DEC-194 (13), opum-doc branch chore/odoc-434-dec-194-13, relayed by the orchestrator. It resolves the ambiguity this task carried and confirms the plan this branch was already built on: (A), proof only, no production change. VERBATIM IN SUBSTANCE: in DEC-194 (5), "required content should mean what the profile pins" meant GRANULARITY - a bare conceptId means the whole document, conceptId#anchor means that section - and NEVER the pinned tier. The pinned tier stays OUT of required: it is admitted against the pack budget as today and is not reserved against the task_evidence cap, because it is not task evidence. (5)s "a ranked Constitution is required WHOLE" is scoped by (13) to the BARE reference. Option B is REJECTED. So the 11-shape measurement stands as the finding, and what was missing was the proof - which is what this branch delivers. The same ruling asks for a Sonnet Stage 1 review at green, which is the orchestrators to dispatch.
finalSummary:
Delivered in opum-ai/lore-cli#608, branch fix/LCLI-731-anchor-scoped-required-content. PROOF ONLY: no production behaviour change. The one src/ edit is a comment.

VALIDATED BY: CI run 38663967879 (pull_request into dev) on commit 2770de5d7bf2b93541ddfaaec24b6a339636e0a7 - 13 jobs success, 1 skipped. The skip is `promotion is manual`, skipped BY DESIGN on a PR into dev by the job that exists to redden PRs into main. Counting by conclusion: 13 success, 1 skipped, 0 failure. Local gates on the same content: `bun run lore check` 0 (0 errors), `bun test` 5147 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail across 151 files, `tsc --noEmit` 0, `biome check .` 0, plus check:packages, check:lockfile-pins and check:breaking-bump all 0.

RULING THAT CLOSED THIS: DEC-194 (13), opum-doc branch chore/odoc-434-dec-194-13, relayed by the orchestrator. It confirms (A) and rejects (B), and it defines (5)s wording as GRANULARITY rather than tier: a bare conceptId means the whole document, conceptId#anchor means that section. The pinned tier stays out of required - admitted against the pack budget, not reserved against the task_evidence cap, because it is not task evidence.

THE FINDING, recorded on this task above with its numbers: the defect this task described does not reproduce. requiredTokens measured over a lopsided Constitution (whole document ~3206 tokens, "## Governance" ~60, "## Principles" ~3111), eleven reference shapes: sources [constitution] 3206; sources [constitution#governance] 60; sources [constitution#principles] 3111; sources [specs/ui] 0; pinned [constitution#governance] + sources [specs/ui] 0; pinned [constitution] + sources [specs/ui] 0; pinned [] with the auto-pin + sources [specs/ui] 0. And the anchored-fits pair the ruling itself names, at ONE 700-token cap: sources [constitution] FAILS with requiredTokens 3202 while sources [constitution#governance] COMPILES holding one 56-token section. WHY: the filter is keyed on candidate.conceptId === constitutionId, but its INPUT is already anchor-shaped, because buildSourceCandidates builds every source candidates through regionForReference(concept.body, reference.anchor) (agent-context.ts:1706). The filer read the filter and not the candidate PRODUCER. A faithful implementation of WHAT TO DO would therefore have been a NO-OP.

WHAT LANDED. Three tests in test/agent-context-budgets.test.ts, both ways: (i) at one cap a ranked constitution#governance compiles while a ranked bare constitution is refused BY NAME with CONTEXT_REQUIRED_CONTENT_OVER_BUDGET, with the positive control in the SAME invocation so the refusal cannot be a fixture artefact; (ii) the anchored reservation is the section size, one item, while its BIG sibling constitution#principles is refused at the same cap, so the cap is genuinely binding; (iii) a ranked bare constitution still reserves the WHOLE document when the cap can hold it, pinned so the behaviour cannot silently narrow. Plus a comment at the required filter in src/core/agent-context.ts recording that its input is already reference-shaped and naming the test file, so the false premise is not re-derived by the next reader. The fixture document is deliberately LOPSIDED so no assertion can pass on rounding.

MUTATION CONTROL, built from the DEFECT shape rather than a fix: make the candidate producer ignore its anchor (regionForReference(concept.body, undefined)), which widens the required set back to the whole document. Predicted subset, measured: exactly the two anchored arms redden and the bare-reference arm stays GREEN. Reverted cleanly.

NO CHANGELOG ENTRY and no docs change, deliberately: there is no user-visible change to document, and the spec already describes the reservation without defining which content is required, so nothing in it is falsified. The four real profiles neither rank nor pin the Constitution, so nothing in the fleet moves.

DEC-182 (1) PATH FLOOR: NOT on it. Changed paths are .quest/tasks/LCLI-731.json, src/core/agent-context.ts and test/agent-context-budgets.test.ts - none is auth/secrets/credentials, permissions/settings, CI workflows or rulesets, package dependencies or lockfiles, install or build hooks, a release or publish path, or the launcher, pins or provider routing. The task carries no security/release/public-surface/design-sensitive label (labels empty, type bug). Closest call, named so it can be overruled rather than discovered: the word "pins" appears in DEC-182 (1)s floor and in this task subject, but there it means the LAUNCHERs version pins and provider routing, not an agent profiles pinned reference array, and this branch changes no profile.
